title: On Keeping the old ledger for forty years
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：keep　|　正文 350 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 keep 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1993 the postman ① kept the old ledger for forty years in public, and every sender in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the postman ② keeps the old ledger for forty years in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ keep the old ledger for forty years at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ kept the old ledger for forty years before — a line in the list for June 1987 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Keeping the old ledger for forty years in public, the postman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the envelope at the far box, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ keep silence all through the day in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Keep silence all through the day at once and never mention it again.

By 2000 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new sender from the next office ⑧ keeps silence all through the day in public every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the box, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ kept the old ledger for forty years again when nobody else would.

⑩ To keep the old ledger for forty years, my mother said in 2005, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody keeps the old ledger for forty years in silence again and somebody must keep the old ledger for forty years in public all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 保存（一般过去式 kept the old ledger for forty years：1993 年邮差头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 保存（一般现在 keeps the old ledger for forty years：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 保存（不定式 to keep the old ledger for forty years：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 保存（过去完成时 had kept the old ledger for forty years：1987 年六月的收发清单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 保存（动名词 keeping the old ledger for forty years 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 保持（keep silence all through the day：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去保持一整天都保持沉默）
G. v. 保持（keep silence all through the day：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 保存（后段两处：新来的寄信人照例 keeps silence all through the day，而母亲又一次 kept the old ledger for forty years）

answers.why: keep 意为“保存”，1993 年邮差当着众人面保存把那本旧簿子留了四十年，那是邮局里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 kept。
keep 意为“保存”，自那以后邮差一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 keeps。
keep 意为“保存”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯保存把那本旧簿子留了四十年”，此处为不定式 to keep the old ledger for forty years。
keep 意为“保存”，收发清单里 六月 那行字说明早在 2000 年之前就有人保存过，故用过去完成时 had kept。
keep 意为“保存”，邮差说“保存把那本旧簿子留了四十年这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 keeping the old ledger for forty years 作主语。
keep 意为“保持”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去保持一整天都保持沉默”，should ever 之后用原形 keep silence all through the day。
keep 意为“保持”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻保持一整天都保持沉默（keep silence all through the day at once），以后再也不要提起。
keep 意为“保存”，新来的寄信人每个星期都照例保持一整天都保持沉默，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 keeps。
keep 意为“保存”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当着众人面保存把那本旧簿子留了四十年，用一般过去式 kept 叙述。
keep 意为“保存”，结尾那句是母亲 2005 年的话：要保存把那本旧簿子留了四十年，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和邮局记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 keep 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1993 the postman kept the old ledger for forty years in public, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the postman keeps the old ledger for forty years in silence whenever the office asks.
Keeping the old ledger for forty years in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever keep silence all through the day in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new sender from the next office keeps silence all through the day in public every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother kept the old ledger for forty years again, and the office remembered that half.
